newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Aug trade figures delayed until Monday.
newsitem.headline: S.African Aug trade figures delayed until Monday.

text.p: Release of South African August trade figures has been delayed until Monday at 1200 GMT to give the Reserve Bank more time to study the data, a South African Revenue Services official said on Friday.
Officials had hoped to release the figures on Friday.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast another healthy trade surplus for August, helping towards a sharp reduction in the current account deficit in the second half of the year.
A repeat of July's exceptional surplus of 2.58 billion rand was ruled out, but all economists predicted a surplus above 500 million rand with the consensus at 760 million rand.
August preliminary money supply figures will be release as scheduled at 1500 GMT on Friday a Reserve Bank official said.
Economists expect year-on-year M3 growth to increase to a consensus 15.7 percent, mainly due to a low comparative period, after dipping to a preliminary 14.69 percent in July from June's 15.65.
Growth in private sector credit extension, however, is seen slowing marginally in August to 17.9 percent from 18.50 in July.
